run.question: Use the custom-crd runbook and check why custom CRD whale-watcher resources are not being reconciled by the operator in namespace app-96

report.summary: The requested runbook does not exist: fetch_skill for skill_id 'custom-crd' returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND and stated the only runbook available for this target is 'service-troubleshooting' (a different entity, not fetched because it does not match a CRD-reconciliation problem), so its steps could not be carried out. Investigating with the available tools: the CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io (group ocean.io, kind WhaleWatcher, Namespaced, v1 served+storage, NamesAccepted and Established True) exists and is healthy, and Deployment whale-operator in namespace app-96 is 1/1 Available with pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-44vgs Running and Ready with 0 restarts (created 07:28:57-07:28:59Z, shortly before the queries ran). The strongest evidence-based finding is a configuration-level blocker: the ServiceAccount app-96/whale-operator is bound (the only binding for it) to ClusterRole whale-operator, whose single rule grants only get/list/watch on ocean.io whalewatchers - no update/patch, no whalewatchers/status, and no rights on any other resource. A controller with only read verbs on its own custom resource cannot persist status or any dependent object, a plausible mechanism for 'resources not being reconciled'; the resulting 403 itself was not observed, so the causal step remains a hypothesis. A second candidate remains open: the CRD's v1 version declares no status subresource, so a controller patching /status would fail regardless of RBAC. No crash, eviction or OOM mechanism was observed.

claims.text: The cluster has one CRD for this API group: customresourcedefinition 'whalewatchers.ocean.io' with group ocean.io, kind WhaleWatcher, plural whalewatchers, singular whalewatcher, scope Namespaced, created 2026-11-21T07:28:57Z, conditions NamesAccepted (reason NoConflicts) and Established (reason InitialNamesAccepted) both True, and version v1 with served=true and storage=true.

The whalewatchers.ocean.io CRD's v1 version definition (spec.versions[0]) contains no 'subresources' field, i.e. no status subresource is declared for WhaleWatcher; its schema only defines spec {depth, location, whaleType} and status {lastSeen, observationCount, phase}.

ClusterRole 'whale-operator' (the only cluster role containing ocean.io/whalewatcher rules) has exactly one rule: apiGroups ["ocean.io"], resources ["whalewatchers"], verbs ["get","list","watch"]. It grants no update, patch, create or delete verb, and no 'whalewatchers/status' or 'whalewatchers/finalizers' resource.

ClusterRoleBinding 'whale-operator' binds ServiceAccount app-96/whale-operator to ClusterRole whale-operator and is the only binding whose subjects include a whale-named subject; a cluster-wide RoleBinding query for subjects matching 'whale' returned no RoleBinding, so no additional namespaced permissions are bound to that ServiceAccount.
ServiceAccount 'whale-operator' exists in namespace app-96 (created 2026-11-21T07:28:57Z), alongside the namespace default ServiceAccount.

Deployment whale-operator in namespace app-96 was created 2026-11-21T07:28:57Z (generation 1, observedGeneration 1) and is 1/1 ready/available with condition Available=True (MinimumReplicasAvailable, lastTransitionTime 2026-11-21T07:28:59Z) and Progressing=True; its container 'operator' runs image python:3.9-slim with command ["python","/app/operator.py"], mounts /app from volume 'operator-code', and sets env OPERATOR_NAMESPACE from fieldRef metadata.namespace.

Pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-44vgs (namespace app-96, owner ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66) is phase Running and Ready=True, its container 'operator' has restartCount 0 and state running startedAt 2026-11-21T07:28:59Z, it runs as serviceAccountName 'whale-operator', and /app is backed by volume 'operator-code' whose source is a Secret (name redacted by the tool).

All 6 events recorded inside the authorized window (queried across all namespaces) belong to namespace app-96 and are Normal: Deployment whale-operator ScalingReplicaSet (scaled replica set whale-operator-5f695b7c66 from 0 to 1, 07:28:57Z), ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66 SuccessfulCreate, and Pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-44vgs Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started between 07:28:57Z and 07:28:59Z.

A cluster-wide ConfigMap query filtered to objects whose name matches whale|ocean|operator or whose data matches whale|ocean.io|whalewatcher returned zero matching objects out of 21 ConfigMaps processed; no operator configuration or fault-injection ConfigMap for the whale operator was found by that query.

Primary hypothesis: WhaleWatcher resources are not reconciled because the operator identity system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator holds only get/list/watch on ocean.io/whalewatchers, so every reconcile write (status update, finalizer, or creation of any dependent object - it holds no rights on any other API group either) is rejected by the API server with 403 Forbidden and no status change is ever persisted. The write attempt itself was not observed, so this causal step is unconfirmed.

Alternative candidate: because CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io declares no status subresource, a controller that patches or updates the /status endpoint would get 404/405 and fail its reconcile loop even if RBAC allowed writes; the operator's reconcile implementation is unknown because its code lives in a Secret that cannot be read.

Alternative candidate: the operator's reconcile loop may never be entered or may be blocked, since the container only started at 2026-11-21T07:28:59Z and its program is supplied from an unreadable Secret; whether /app/operator.py runs a working watch loop cannot be confirmed from its code, and its log stream yielded no lines in this Run so no error text was readable.

The operator workload itself looks healthy and no crash mechanism is visible: Deployment whale-operator is 1/1 available, pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-44vgs is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and container state running, and none of the 6 in-window events is a Warning (no FailedScheduling, BackOff, Unhealthy, OOMKilled or Evicted). The pod was created 07:28:57-07:28:59Z as the first ReplicaSet (generation 1), i.e. a fresh deployment rather than a restart of an existing template.

Rejected as the cause: a pod failure, OOMKill, eviction or scheduling problem on the operator. The operator pod is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and container state running, and the in-window event set for app-96 contains only Normal reasons (ScalingReplicaSet, SuccessfulCreate, Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started) with no Evicted, OOMKilling, BackOff or FailedScheduling.

Advice: extend ClusterRole whale-operator so the reconciler can write - add verbs update/patch on ocean.io whalewatchers and, if a status subresource is added, on whalewatchers/status (plus permissions for whatever dependent resources the operator must create), and consider declaring spec.versions[0].subresources.status in the whalewatchers.ocean.io CRD so status writes use the /status endpoint. Re-check WhaleWatcher status.phase/observationCount afterwards to confirm reconciliation.

gaps: The named runbook 'custom-crd' does not exist for this target: fetch_skill returned status error KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND and listed only 'service-troubleshooting' (a different entity, not fetched because it does not match a CRD-reconciliation problem). No custom-crd step could be carried out; the missing skill is the tool/document gap.

WhaleWatcher custom resources could not be read: kind 'whalewatchers' is not an allowed kind for the Kubernetes tools, so kubernetes_jq_query returned INVALID_PARAMS for kind=whalewatchers in namespace app-96. Whether the CRs exist, in which namespace they live, and their status.phase are unknown.

The operator log query returned no lines: fetch_pod_logs for whale-operator-5f695b7c66-44vgs returned status no_data with 0 lines (current instance read, previous instance not found) for both the 07:28:00-07:29:36Z window (evidence_id a80a624f-012b-4ba5-b5d3-c40fe2348af0-t0:3bed247f-b9e5-4451-88f1-e454ab951d82) and the default hour (89065ce9-fd8c-49c1-9539-9ab184b39221-t0:fd19f295-31a0-4bb5-9aa9-155d56318e30); these views are limits of what was observed, not evidence of absence, so no 403 Forbidden or other reconcile error text could be read.

Prometheus was unavailable during this Run (get_metric_names and get_prometheus_target returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate, restart or custom operator metric could be checked; metric evidence is unknown rather than zero.

The operator's source code is delivered from volume 'operator-code' backed by a Secret; Secrets cannot be read, so I could not verify what the operator does (whether it writes status, patches /status, or creates child resources).

NetworkPolicy objects across all namespaces returned no_data, and ResourceQuota in app-96 also returned no_data (8d3c6630-e7fd-4c3a-b939-83473cec6b8e-t0:c6a1933a-9060-486d-901d-c16dab9d3a7c, 8d3c6630-e7fd-4c3a-b939-83473cec6b8e-t2:9c3d3510-9478-4b40-b9d5-b09e716cc13e); their absence and any connectivity or quota contribution are therefore unconfirmed.

No audit-log or apiserver change source is available in this Run (change_history is not integrated), so I could not confirm an actual 403 Forbidden from system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator, nor when the ClusterRole and its binding were authored; objects are visible only in their current state.
next_steps: For a human with audit-log access: check apiserver audit entries for user system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator on resource whalewatchers (verbs update/patch, or path .../status) in namespace app-96 around and after 2026-11-21T07:28:57Z to confirm or refute the 403 hypothesis.
Inspect the WhaleWatcher objects (kubectl get whalewatchers -n app-96 -o yaml) and their status.phase/observationCount/lastSeen to see whether any status was ever written.

Review the Secret 'operator-code' referenced by Deployment whale-operator to confirm whether the controller writes status via updateStatus (which would also require a status subresource) or via main-resource update.
Compare with a known-good operator deployment in this lab to see whether an update/patch grant on <resource>/status is normally present.
